page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a substantial 15,359 GB of local storage that is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

In performance evaluations, the L64as_v4 demonstrates strong capabilities, particularly in multi-core processing. It achieved a top-tier rating in the Geekbench multi-core benchmark and a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are strong, large-block uncached read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores fall into the average tier. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES.

This server configuration is highly suited for large-scale database operations, data warehousing, and high-throughput web serving, as evidenced by its strong Passmark database and Redis SET benchmark results. The massive 15.3 TB local storage capacity combined with a high-density memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive workloads that require local caching or large working sets without the latency of external storage. It also supports moderate LLM inference tasks, showing top-tier prompt processing speeds for smaller models.
description: The Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this Hyper-V-managed instance includes 15,359 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with strong ratings in database operations, Redis SET transactions, and static web serving. While memory bandwidth for small-block cached reads is strong, uncached large-block reads perform at an average level. The server's high storage-to-vCPU density and balanced memory allocation make it qualitatively cost-effective for data-intensive workloads. It is highly recommended for large databases, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
